A.name: PC5 Native
A.objective: An installable, PlayStation-inspired PC operating system on qualified mainstream x86-64 hardware.

B.name: Prospero
B.objective: Evidence-backed research into PS5 executable compatibility and genuine PS5 system-software execution, isolated from Track A's release path.

milestones.title: Architecture freeze and repository audit
acceptance: every tracked file is classified in the repository audit, with measured counts rather than estimates
the dual-track boundary is recorded as ADR-010 and enforced by tests/test_architecture.py
the Linux-foundation decision is recorded as ADR-009 with its exit condition and current blocker
documentation drift found by the audit is corrected or explicitly filed
the milestone graph in docs/architecture/roadmap.json validates with zero errors
make check passes with the architecture tests included
milestones.next_action: M1a is already proven; start M1c hardening (OVMF run) and M1 installer design in parallel.

milestones.title: Reproducible BIOS boot medium
acceptance: make iso produces build/pc5.iso reproducibly under SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
make verify passes every structural check
make boot-test boots the image on the v86/SeaBIOS emulated PC and asserts the rendered interface
the kernel mounts its own medium through its ATAPI/ISO9660 driver

milestones.title: Automated CI and release publication
milestones.blocker: GitHub App installation lacks the Workflows permission, so ci/build.yml cannot be pushed to .github/workflows/; see ci/README.md.
acceptance: the workflow file is registered under .github/workflows/ and appears in gh api repos/.../actions/workflows
a tag push builds twice, requires identical hashes, runs every suite and publishes exactly three assets
a failed test run publishes nothing

milestones.title: UEFI boot path under real firmware
acceptance: the loader's logic is executed end to end against the stub firmware (42 checks) — done
the same BOOTX64.EFI boots under OVMF and the serial log is recorded — NOT done
one physical UEFI machine reaches the PC5 kernel with Secure Boot off and the log is committed — NOT done
GOP-only machines get a working framebuffer console and the text fallback is no longer required
milestones.next_action: Obtain OVMF (or a UEFI-capable VM) in the build environment; a stub run may never be relabelled as firmware compatibility.

milestones.title: ATA PIO storage write path (emulated HDD)
deliverables: kernel/ata.c (device-indexed 512-byte sector read/write, LBA28, cache flush)
kernel/storage_test.c (explicit write self-test on a reserved window)
tests/boot_test.py (write, read-back, guard and host-side image checks)
acceptance: writes take an explicit device index; no call falls back to the selected boot device
ATAPI devices, zero counts, out-of-range or overflowing LBAs, invalid indices and NULL buffers are refused with distinct statuses
a 4 KiB deterministic pattern is written to a reserved 8-sector window, cache-flushed, read back and compared
the kernel's SHA-256 of the read-back equals the host's SHA-256 of the same bytes in the emulator's disk image
nothing outside the scratch window is written, and the CD-ROM path still boots and mounts ISO9660 with the disk attached
the write test never runs on an ordinary boot; it requires the explicit serial command
physical disk writing is NOT included and is not claimed
milestones.next_action: Repeat the write on the REF-AMD physical machine; then a partition-table parser and a writable filesystem behind the same sector interface.

milestones.title: Physical boot and installation
deliverables: bootable USB image (isohybrid MBR plus UEFI entry)
acceptance: all three reference configurations boot from USB and each records a complete PC5-LOG and screen dump
the installer writes to NVMe on the AMD reference machine and to SATA on the Intel reference machine
the installed system boots with the installation medium removed
the recovery entry boots on the same machine and can reinstall
evidence for each machine is committed under docs/evidence/m1/<machine>/ with the firmware version and Secure Boot state
milestones.next_action: Sector write (M1d), partition discovery (M1e) and read-only FAT32 (M1f) exist. Next: FAT32 write, then the installer and isohybrid USB medium; AHCI/NVMe follow behind the same sector interface.

milestones.title: Read-only MBR and GPT partition discovery
deliverables: kernel/part.c (pure MBR/GPT parsers, CRC-32, explicit-device scan)
kernel/main.c (boot-time scan, PC5-LOG evidence, never fatal)
tests/disk_images.py (reproducible MBR/GPT fixtures, including a damaged table)
tests/boot_test.py (GPT disk, damaged-table refusal, blank-disk negative)
acceptance: a GPT disk is parsed read-only from its protective MBR, header and entry array; header and entry CRCs are verified
a table with a mismatched CRC is refused with status=crc and the boot continues
a blank disk is reported as scheme=none status=signature, not as an empty table
partitions that overlap or extend past the device are refused with a distinct status
the scan takes an explicit device index and refuses ATAPI before reading a sector
no write, format or mount call exists in the partition module
extended/logical MBR partitions are labelled as not walked rather than guessed
milestones.next_action: Writable filesystem on a discovered partition (task A in the next three), then the installer.

milestones.title: Read-only FAT32 filesystem
deliverables: kernel/fat32.c (BPB validation, FAT chains, root directory, 8.3 lookup, file read)
kernel/include/pc5.h (volume, entry and status types; injected sector reader)
kernel/main.c (mount on the discovered, explicitly indexed disk; PC5-LOG evidence)
kernel/ui.c (`ls` and `read` commands, storage-page filesystem line)
tests/fat32_images.py (deterministic FAT32 fixture and an independent reader)
tests/fat32_check.c (host driver: kernel module reads the fixture, prints digests)
tests/test_fat32.py (three-way SHA-256 comparison and refusal contracts)
tests/boot_test.py (emulated mount, list, read, digest and image-unchanged checks)
acceptance: a FAT32 partition is mounted read-only through the M1e partition table on an explicit disk index
BPB and geometry are validated before any traversal; FAT12/FAT16 volumes are refused structurally
free, bad, reserved, out-of-range and cyclic cluster chains are refused with distinct statuses
files are read through multi-cluster and fragmented chains, with partial final clusters and zero-length files
the kernel's SHA-256 for every fixture file equals both the generated bytes and an independent reader's digest
the disk image is byte-identical before and after reading
no write path exists in the filesystem module and ATAPI is never mounted
long file names are skipped by design, not parsed on a guess
milestones.next_action: FAT32 write (M1g): create, flush, independent read-back.

milestones.title: Safe FAT32 write: create, flush, independent read-back
deliverables: kernel/fat32.c (fat32_create_file: allocation, FAT copies, FSInfo, directory entry, bounded write order, read-back)
kernel/include/pc5.h (write/flush callbacks, write report, stage enum, new refusal statuses)
kernel/ata.c (ata_flush: explicit FLUSH CACHE on an explicit device, ATAPI refused)
kernel/ui.c (`put NAME.EXT text` command and storage-page write line)
tests/fat32_write_check.c (host driver with deterministic payload and write/flush fault injection)
tests/test_fat32_write.py (36 tests: creation matrix, refusals, FSInfo, flush, fault injection, harness safety)
tests/fat32_images.py (independent reader plus structural checks: FAT copies, chains, orphans, FSInfo, changed sectors)
tests/boot_test.py (create in the emulator, dumped image read back by the independent reader)
acceptance: an explicitly mounted FAT32 volume on an explicitly indexed ATA disk gains one new 8.3 root file
clusters are chosen from free FAT entries only, with the allocator refusing instead of overwriting
every FAT copy is written and then re-read, and a divergent mirror is reported rather than assumed
the FSInfo block is validated before use; an implausible block is neither trusted nor rewritten
the file's bytes, FAT chain, directory entry and FSInfo counters are all confirmed by an independent FAT32 reader
every pre-existing file still reads back byte for byte, and both FAT copies remain identical
changed sectors are confined to the allocated data, the FATs, the FSInfo blocks and the root directory
existing names, full volumes, full root directories, invalid names, read-only sources and oversize files are refused without writing
write, flush and corruption failures leave a documented state (intact, leaked chain or reported inconsistency), never a silent success
reads remain unchanged and the boot path never attaches a write callback
milestones.next_action: Physical boot and the installer (M2), starting with overwrite/rename and directory creation.

milestones.title: Hybrid MBR: the same ISO boots as a hard disk
deliverables: boot/mbr.S (440-byte MBR bootstrap: relay at 0x0500, INT 13h extended read, hand-off at 0000:7C00 with DL preserved)
tools/mkiso.py (hybrid MBR composition from the real layout: patch words, disk signature, one whole-image partition, CHS, 55AA)
tools/verify_iso.py (independent MBR verification: signature, one entry, type/flag/extent, CHS, patch words, no overlap, nothing past EOF)
tests/test_hybrid.py (37 tests: assembled bootstrap bytes, layout, determinism, and a rejection test per corruption)
tests/boot_test.py (boots the ISO with no CD attached, plus a blanked-sector-0 control)
Makefile (build/mbr.bin pinned to 440 bytes, passed as --mbr-code)
acceptance: the image carries a valid MBR in the ISO9660 system area: 55AA at 510, a disk signature, one partition entry with the boot flag set and type 0x17
the partition describes the actual image: start LBA 0, length = every 512-byte sector of the file, nothing past the end, no overlap, CHS consistent with the LBA fields
the MBR bootstrap loads the same boot image El Torito names, using values patched in from the layout rather than a template
the El Torito entries, the ISO9660 layout, the 4096-byte stage-1 loader and the FAT ESP are unchanged
the verifier rejects every inconsistency it can express, and a test per corruption proves it
the image boots with the CD detached and the disk attached, reaching the same kernel build as the CD path
a copy with sector 0 blanked does not boot at all, so the evidence is not an artefact of the firmware falling back
two clean builds remain byte-identical, and the MBR path adds no firmware binary and no kernel change
milestones.next_action: Physical boot on a real machine with a USB stick (M2); then overwrite/rename and directory creation for the installer.

milestones.title: Hardware abstraction and drivers
deliverables: Linux-kernel-based hardware support for the qualified device set
PC5 hardware abstraction layer over display, input, storage, audio and network
Ethernet and Wi-Fi enablement per qualified device
acceptance: every reference configuration has a compatibility-matrix row with boot, GPU acceleration, storage, USB, audio and network results measured separately
the DualSense is enumerated and its input reports are dumped and committed (buttons, sticks, touchpad, motion, adaptive triggers)
GPU acceleration is demonstrated by a recorded renderer string and a rendered frame on each GPU vendor
no device is described as supported without a row that names the measurement
milestones.next_action: Produce the qualification-matrix template as machine-readable rows before writing driver code, so results cannot be invented later.

milestones.title: PC5 operating system
deliverables: PC5 system image (immutable base plus update slots)
acceptance: a clean install reaches the PC5 home screen on every reference configuration without a keyboard
an application can be installed, launched, suspended and removed from the PC5 interface
an interrupted update leaves a bootable system in the previous slot
the image build is reproducible from a recorded commit and SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH
milestones.next_action: Define the system-image composition and the session boundary before choosing shell technology.

milestones.title: PlayStation experience
deliverables: DualSense feature integration (light bar, haptics, adaptive triggers)
system settings and account-free profile handling
acceptance: every shell surface is reachable and operable with a DualSense alone; the keyboard is optional
DualSense features are individually exercised and the report/effect evidence is committed
the library launches a registered title and returns to the shell with state preserved
input-to-photon latency is measured on each reference configuration and recorded
milestones.next_action: Prototype the shell against the M3 session API on one machine before generalising.

milestones.title: PS5 executable compatibility (research and runtime)
deliverables: PS5 ELF/SELF intake analysis with documented, lawful input requirements
loader and relocation support for user-space executables
PRX/NID import resolution with independently implemented shims
graphics and audio translation boundary for relinked titles
acceptance: at least one lawfully obtained PS5 user-space executable reaches a recorded, reproducible execution milestone (entry, syscall loop or presented frame) on PC5 Native
the record names the milestone reached and never describes it as PS5 system software or firmware execution
each attempted title has a row with the blocking subsystem, or the milestone is recorded as not reached
no Sony firmware, key or proprietary library is required, redistributed or derived
milestones.next_action: Host-side feasibility spike on a machine that can build the relinker, recorded as a negative or positive result.

milestones.title: Genuine Prospero research
deliverables: firmware structure research on lawfully obtained images (never distributed)
acceptance: a feasibility report cites public evidence for every claim and states what remains unproven
the hardware dependency map names each SoC block a PC would have to emulate
the legal assessment is written by or reviewed against counsel-grade sources before any experiment
the report ends in an explicit go / no-go recommendation; no stage of the PC5 compatibility chain is advanced by research alone
milestones.next_action: Legal assessment first; the technical feasibility question is not worth funding before it is answered.

milestones.title: Performance and compatibility expansion
deliverables: GPU, storage and controller latency measurements
acceptance: the benchmark suite runs unattended on every reference configuration and produces comparable records
a compatibility database row exists for every tested machine and title, generated from measurements
crash reports are attributable to a component and reproduce from the recorded configuration
no performance number is published without the machine, build and command that produced it
milestones.next_action: Define the benchmark manifest and evidence format in M2 so early runs already produce reusable data.

milestones.title: Release-quality PC5
deliverables: reproducible release pipeline and published assets
acceptance: a tagged commit builds twice to identical artifacts and publishes exactly the documented asset set
the update signature is verified before apply and a corrupted update is refused
a power cut during an update leaves a bootable, recoverable system
every machine on the qualification list has a committed evidence record from the release build
milestones.next_action: Blocked behind M7 and the Workflows permission that M1b needs; do not schedule a release before qualification exists.
